summary: Cart minus (decrement) button has no lower bound: it allows item quantities to go to 0 and then into negative values. On cart.html, repeatedly clicking "−" on Garlic Bread took the quantity from 2 → 1 → 0 → -1 → -2, producing line totals of "$0.00" and "$-4.99" / "$-9.98". Expected behaviour is to clamp at 1, or to remove the line item once the quantity would drop below 1. Instead the cart displays a nonsensical negative item count and a negative line total that can subtract from the order total.

summary: Stale cart summary: clicking the minus (or plus) button re-renders the individual cart row (quantity and line total update), but the grand total, the "You have N items in your cart" headline, and the header cart badge are NOT recalculated. While the Garlic Bread line total changed from $9.98 to $-9.98, the summary Total stayed frozen at $28.73 and the badge/headline stayed at "4 items". This means the displayed Total no longer equals the sum of the visible line totals.

evidence.content:
On http://127.0.0.1:5500/cart.html, after each click of button.dec[data-id="garlic-bread"], the row updated but the summary did not: Visible line totals after 4 decrement clicks: $-9.98 (Garlic Bread), $6.25 (Truffle Fries), $12.50 (Margherita Pizza) => actual sum = $8.77 Summary/badge rendered each time (unchanged from page load): $28.73 4

You have 4 items in your cart

Expected after decrements: Total = $23.74, $18.75, $13.76, $8.77 progressively, and headline/badge reflecting the item count. The Total, headline, and badge were identical in every snapshot, i.e. renderRows() updates #cart-rows but never recomputes #cart-total / #cart-headline / #cart-badge (or the dec/inc handler skips the summary render step).
